parsed.why: No criminalisation of trans expression; constitutional protection, court-issued police guidelines, and 2026 relief on passport medical exams show functioning recourse, offset by documented airport, railway and custody friction and a hostile 2026 recognition amendment.

No trans-specific offence or documented police or border targeting, and functioning institutions, but no anti-discrimination or hate-crime law, deep social conservatism, and only one indigenous third-gender acceptance data point: open questions plus thin recourse hold it down.

Enforced sodomy statute applied to arrest trans people for gender expression (2026), police forced genital display and public outing, official and religious hostility, blocked LGBT groups, no recognition, care or recourse: state-tolerated targeting with severe consequences.

Decriminalisation by 2024 reading-down is positive, but no trans-specific law, protection or data exists; documented violence, slurs against gender-nonconforming people, and police refusal to investigate LGBT victims show hostility with thin recourse, though mainly dated.

Decriminalisation upheld, constitutional sexual-orientation protection, a 2024 harassment act covering gender identity, Pride and high regional acceptance support safety; an immigration statute listing homosexuals and government and religious hostility, plus unenforced pledges and thin trans data, hold it back.
